title: Licence plate prefix 'WP': Western Province
description: The two letters before the registration number give the province where the vehicle was registered: 'WP' is the Western Province (WP Western, NP Northern, NC North-Central, EP Eastern, NW North-Western, CP Central, UP Uva, SG Sabaragamuwa, SP Southern). Useful when plates are unblurred.

title: Tamil first on signs: north and east
description: Apart from English, the official languages are Sinhala and Tamil. A monolingual Tamil sign, or a bilingual sign with Tamil first or on top, points to the Tamil-speaking areas: the north, the east coast and parts of the central hills.

title: Sinhala first on signs: south, west and centre
description: Apart from English, the official languages are Sinhala and Tamil. A monolingual Sinhala sign, or a bilingual sign with Sinhala first or on top, points to the Sinhala-speaking majority of the country: the west, south and centre.

title: Gen 4 'shitcam' (North-Central and Western)
description: Low-quality Gen 4 'shitcam' coverage is found in most of the North-Central Province and the Western Province (research by Yaron).

title: Gen 3 smudge on the car (north and north-west)
description: In Gen 3 coverage, a round smudge is visible at the top left of the front of the car in most of northern and north-western Sri Lanka. Much of this coverage has since been overwritten by Gen 4.

title: Mountains: south-central Sri Lanka
description: Sri Lanka is mostly flat to rolling coastal plains; mountains are found only in the south-central part of the island.

title: Palmyra palms (north and east)
description: Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) are extremely common in the north and east of Sri Lanka.

title: Coconut plantations: the Coconut Triangle
description: Coconut plantations are very common in the Puttalam, Kurunegala and Gampaha districts (the 'Coconut Triangle'), but can also appear further south. Coconut trees grow all over the country; it is the plantations that are region-specific.

title: Lowland rainforest with dark red soil
description: Lowland rainforests, with lush vegetation and dark red soil, in the south-west (above all Ratnapura, also Kalutara, Galle, Matara and Kegalle).

title: Montane rainforest (Nuwara Eliya)
description: Montane rainforests, with twisted, more 'cold-climate looking' vegetation, in the highlands (above all Nuwara Eliya district, also Kandy).

title: Tea plantations (central and south-west)
description: Tea plantations are found mostly in the centre and south-west. The accompanying type of forest (lowland or montane rainforest) helps to regionguess further.

title: Areca palms in forested areas (Ratnapura, Galle, Matara)
description: Areca palms are very common in forested areas of Ratnapura district and the northern parts of Galle and Matara districts. They are much taller than other palms, with a very narrow trunk. They also grow in urban areas and gardens elsewhere, so use with caution and look for other clues.

title: Horton Plains National Park
description: Horton Plains National Park is very distinct, with a foggy climate and wide open grassland.

title: Flat, dry land with light brown soil (west of Yala)
description: The area west of Yala National Park is very flat and dry, with characteristic light brown soil.

title: Dry landscape with reddish soil (North-Central)
description: The North-Central Province and the southern part of the Northern Province look dry, like the area west of Yala, but can be told apart by the more reddish soil.

title: Flat farmland, water bodies and isolated ridges (Batticaloa–Pottuvil)
description: The east coast between Batticaloa and Pottuvil is very flat and agricultural, with many water bodies and small streams; isolated mountains or ridges are often visible.

title: Fences of dead leaves and corrugated iron (north and east)
description: Walls and fences made of dead palm leaves and corrugated iron sheets are very common in the north and east. They often coincide with the distribution of palmyra palms.

title: Sandy gravel road shoulders (Mannar)
description: Sandy gravel on either side of the road on Mannar Island and in the adjacent mainland area. Needs more research — use with caution.

title: E01 expressway kilometre markers
description: The only divided highways in Sri Lanka are the expressways (E roads), which carry regular blue markers with the distance in km from their starting point. E01 starts from Homagama near Colombo, so the distance grows as you go south.

title: E02 expressway kilometre markers
description: The only divided highways in Sri Lanka are the expressways (E roads), with regular blue km markers. E02 also starts from Homagama, so the distance grows as you go north.

title: E03 expressway with a hedgerow in the middle
description: E03 starts in the north of Colombo; its km markers grow going north, and most of the road has a distinct hedgerow in the central reservation.

title: E06 expressway kilometre markers
description: E06 starts from Mattala airport; the km markers grow the further south you go towards Hambantota. (E04 has no coverage.)

title: European-looking houses and terraces (Nuwara Eliya)
description: The architecture in and around Nuwara Eliya looks distinct and more European than in the rest of the country; terraced hillsides with cultivation and houses are also common here.

title: Blue tsunami evacuation route signs (Trincomalee)
description: These blue tsunami evacuation route signs are often found in Trincomalee.
